absent: Contracts and failure codes of internal insertion request release and intersect helpers.
Allocation lifetime and flag effects for resource handles.
Complete field layout and valid value encodings for resource attributes and descriptors.
Creation and lifetime of global roots guards wait queues and persistent inode.
Device resource framework attachment detachment and action semantics.
Boot argument parsing helpers and reserved table publication.
Iteration order and pruning guarantees of hierarchy walkers and list helpers.
Mapping revocation effects and allowance policy for physical ranges.
Scheduling and wakeup behavior for multiplexed sharing.
Exact log formats stack dump triggers and warning conditions beyond observed calls.

findings.text: Offers a root insertion operation for a detached entry that widens the requested interval to include any conflicting entry and retries until it fits or meets the root itself; already linked entries are left untouched.

Offers removal and repositioning of an existing entry; repositioning only succeeds when the replacement interval remains inside the parent, keeps sibling ordering and continues to enclose all descendants.

Offers reservation of an interval under a root with automatic subdivision around busy portions, marking created pieces busy with the root type; the public wrapper clamps partially outside requests to the root and abandons disjoint ones.
Reports an alignment value derived from mode flags: extent based, start based, or zero when neither mode is selected.
Exposes the address space of the persistent iomem inode for file open paths, relying on an acquire barrier against early revocation races.
Provides allocation plus locked insertion of a named interval under a parent, descending through transparent containers and waiting for multiplexed owners before reporting busy.
Provides removal of an exact busy interval under a parent, descending through transparent containers and waking multiplexed waiters when the freed entry was shareable.
Provides adjustable release of a memory interval that frees, shrinks or bisects the enclosing busy memory entry and redistributes affected descendants between the resulting halves.
Provides marking of a system memory busy entry as mergeable and coalescing with adjacent compatible neighbors, freeing the absorbed entry.
Provides device bound resource ownership where a conflict check precedes attachment and device teardown automatically releases the entry; equality is by stored pointer.
Provides device bound interval ownership keyed by parent together with start and length, with automatic release on teardown and explicit release by matching key.

Provides sanity and exclusivity queries over the iomem hierarchy, list entry allocation with embedded fallback plus safe list disposal, and discovery of a disjoint free memory interval for device or anonymous use.
Boot option handler consumes start length pairs and installs up to a small bounded count of reserved entries, classifying low addresses as port space and others as memory.
Device interval tracking record carries a parent handle together with start offset and length, used as both release argument and match key.
List wrapper carries a list node plus a resource pointer that either references a supplied entry or an embedded spare, supporting uniform disposal.
Hierarchy preserves containment with ordered disjoint siblings; transparent entries are traversed rather than treated as terminal owners, and busy marks terminal ownership.

Bounds changes preserve enclosure: a new interval must fit the parent, avoid neighbors and still cover children; memory coalescing additionally requires identical attributes, adjacency and childlessness.
Alignment reporting is determined solely by the two mode bits, yielding extent, start or zero with no other inputs.
Free scan direction determines origin and stepping: ascending from aligned lower bound, descending from capped upper bound, with wrap aware termination.

Mutating operations hold the global resource write guard across search plus link or unlink, including expand to fit, remove, adjust, split reservation, locked request, release, adjustable release and memory merge.

Inspection paths hold the read guard while walking; multiplexed acquisition temporarily drops the write guard while sleeping and reacquires before retry, with wakeup issued after unlink outside the guard.

Split reservation cycles among attempt, absorb fully covered remainder, trim leading overlap, or carve leading piece plus queue trailing remainder, ending when no remainder remains or allocation fails.
Locked request cycles among configure from parent, attempt, descend through transparent conflict, warn on special device memory clash, wait on multiplexed sharing, or fail.
Adjustable release selects among free whole, shrink either edge, or bisect with spare creation and child redistribution; merge then attempts successor coalescing followed by predecessor coalescing.

Free discovery iterates candidate origins, skips intersecting windows, then either completes a locked iomem claim with mapping revocation or completes a childless insertion under the base, otherwise reports out of range.

Early revocation before inode publication is silently ignored; relaxed allowance at both ends also skips unmapping, otherwise the full extent is unmapped. Two build variants exist: active revocation versus no operation.

Out of range reservation logs and dumps stack; freeing a missing interval warns; merging a non memory busy entry warns; adjustment failures during release warn; allocation exhaustion retries with stronger guarantees or aborts the split.
Two option bits control free search: one selects descending order and one selects locked region request semantics.
Default alignment has two build dependent values: section shift derived versus page sized.
Boot reservation table holds four entries maximum.
Strict iomem enforcement flag has two build dependent initial states: enabled versus disabled.
